subject: language_arts

unit.title: Apostrophes & homophones
unit.essentialQuestion: When does a word need an apostrophe, and how do I pick between sound-alike words?

title: Apostrophes job 1: squashing words (contractions)
objectives: By the end, I can write a contraction with the apostrophe where letters are missing.

vocabulary.definition: the tiny floating mark ( ' ) that does special jobs in words
two words squashed into one, with some letters dropped
the letters that fall out when two words get squashed
vocabulary.example: the o of not disappears in don't

emphasize: The apostrophe stands EXACTLY where the letters went missing — like a little gravestone marking the gap.
The move: find the missing letters → put the apostrophe there.
Pre-empt the wrong-spot apostrophe (do'nt) and the missing one (cant).

keyConcepts: contraction = two words squashed into one
letters drop out when we squash
the apostrophe marks the exact spot where letters went missing
misconceptions: apostrophe placed at the join of the two words instead of where letters dropped (do'nt)
leaving the apostrophe out entirely (cant, dont)
keeping the dropped letters AND adding an apostrophe (I'am)
hooks: Bury the missing letters under a tiny apostrophe gravestone — we squash words like this every day when we talk.
priorKnowledge: the child already says don't and I'm naturally in speech

digital: animated whiteboard (crossing out dropped letters in red)

video.title: Sing with Grammarsaurus - Apostrophes
video.watchTask: Every time the song squashes two words together, shout out which letters went missing BEFORE the apostrophe appears.

afterCheck.question: In a contraction, what does the apostrophe stand in place of?
afterCheck.expectedAnswer: The missing letters (the ones that dropped out when the words were squashed)

plan.goal: Frame the apostrophe as a tiny gravestone marking where squashed-out letters are buried; connect to how the child already talks.
plan.note: Keep it playful — the gravestone image carries the whole lesson. Retrieve natural speech contractions.
plan.successCriteria: Child says a natural sentence with don't or I'm and notices letters 'fall out' when we squash.

script.say: When we talk fast, we squash words together. Do not becomes don't. But look — some letters fall out when we squash! Where did the o in not go? We mark the gap with a tiny apostrophe — like a little gravestone showing where the letters are buried. Let's bury some letters! Quick question first: do you ever say don't or I'm when you talk? Say me a sentence with don't.
script.adaptHints: Listen for natural use, e.g. 'I don't like spiders' — echo it back warmly. If unsure, model: 'I am hungry → I'm hungry. People squash words all the time when they speak.' Swap the example sentence topic for the child's interests.

elements.value: the ' is buried where the o was!

stuckProtocol: If no contraction comes naturally: say 'I am hungry' fast three times — hear it turn into 'I'm hungry'? That squash is a contraction.

plan.goal: Model the move on three contractions: squash the words, cross the dropped letters in red, put the apostrophe exactly in the gap.
plan.note: Same three-step routine each time: write both words → cross the dropped letter(s) → apostrophe in their exact place.
plan.successCriteria: Child can point to where the apostrophe sits in don't, I'm and it's and say it marks the missing letters.

script.say: Job one of the apostrophe: squashing words. Watch do not. I squash them: donot — too long. The o in not drops out. The apostrophe takes its place: don't. The apostrophe sits EXACTLY where the letter went missing. Now I am: squash to Iam, the a drops out — I'm. And it is: the i drops out — it's. Find the missing letter, put the apostrophe there.
script.adaptHints: Repeat the rule rhythmically: 'find the missing letters, bury them with the apostrophe.' Keep each squash quick and dramatic.

blocks.caption: The apostrophe marks the spot where the letters went missing.

plan.goal: Shared squashing: the child finds the dropped letters for can not, she will and we are, then matches contractions to their long forms.
plan.note: Child supplies the missing letters; character confirms and places the apostrophe. Finish with the matching block.
plan.successCriteria: Child names the buried letters in can't (the n and o of not) and matches all four pairs.

script.say: Squash these with me. Can not — which letters drop out? The n and the o of not! So it becomes can't. Now she will — the w-i drops — she'll. And we are — the a drops — we're. Your turn: match each squashed word to the two words it came from. Then tell me — in can't, which letters did we bury?
script.adaptHints: Point to where each apostrophe sits as the child matches. If they hesitate, un-squash the contraction out loud: 'can't… caaan nnnot.'

blocks.prompt: Match each contraction to the two words it was squashed from.

check.question: In can't, which letters did we bury?
check.expectedAnswer: The n and o of not — the apostrophe stands in their place

wrongAnswers.why: thinks the last letter merged or vanished
wrongAnswers.remedy: Say can't slowly — the t is still there at the end! Which bit of 'not' can you NOT hear any more?

wrongAnswers.answer: no letters — it just glues the words
wrongAnswers.why: thinks the apostrophe is a glue mark at the join, not a gap marker
wrongAnswers.remedy: Write can not, then can't underneath. Compare letter by letter — which two letters disappeared?

plan.goal: Diagnostic: contract cannot — placement of the apostrophe is the key evidence.
plan.note: The wrong options are the two classic errors: apostrophe at the join (ca'nt) and no apostrophe (cant).
plan.successCriteria: Child picks can't and can say which letters the apostrophe replaces.

script.say: Your inspector moment. Contract cannot into one word. Think: which letters fall out, and where must the apostrophe sit?
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'Which letters are missing, and is the apostrophe sitting in their spot?'

blocks.explain: The n and o of not drop out, and the apostrophe stands exactly in their place: can't.

wrongAnswers.why: apostrophe at the join or the end, not where the letters dropped
wrongAnswers.remedy: Where did the letters drop out? In not — the n and o go. The apostrophe goes right there: can't.

wrongAnswers.why: forgot the gravestone — no apostrophe at all
wrongAnswers.remedy: Letters went missing — we must mark the gap. Where did they go? Put the apostrophe there.

plan.goal: Independent squashing: the child writes contractions for word pairs, always naming the buried letters.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Ask 'which letters did you bury?' after each answer — it is the self-check habit.
plan.successCriteria: Child writes 3+ contractions with the apostrophe correctly placed where letters were dropped.

script.say: Practice time, letter-burier! I'll give you word pairs — you squash them, and every time, point to the spot where the letters got buried.
script.adaptHints: Frame sentences with the child's interests (pets, football, dinosaurs). Never change the target contractions.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'let's find which letters fall out.'
Step down: cross the dropped letters together in red first.
ONE hint: 'the apostrophe goes exactly where you crossed out.'
Re-ask a smaller version (one pair, e.g. I am → I'm).
Keep it safe: 'Apostrophes hide where letters used to be — let's hunt for the gap.'

plan.goal: Child states the apostrophe's first job and where it sits; end on a win.
plan.note: Child-led; the character listens. Process praise only.
plan.successCriteria: Child says: it squashes two words into one, and the apostrophe sits where the missing letters were.

script.say: Tell me the apostrophe's first job, and where it sits. … Exactly — squashing words, and the apostrophe stands right where the letters went missing. You found the missing letters every time and put the apostrophe right on the spot — that's exactly how contractions work.
script.adaptHints: Tease tomorrow: 'the apostrophe has a SECOND job — it can show who owns things. See you then!'

practiceBank.skill: write a contraction with the apostrophe in the gap

wrongAnswers.why: left out the apostrophe — the gap is unmarked
wrongAnswers.remedy: A letter went missing — the a of am. We must mark the gap. Where does the apostrophe go?

wrongAnswers.why: added the apostrophe but kept the dropped letter
wrongAnswers.remedy: If the a is still there, nothing went missing! Cross the a out first — THEN the apostrophe takes its place.

hints: Squash I and am — which letter falls out?
The a of am drops. Put the apostrophe exactly in its spot.

reteach.say: Watch the squash in slow motion: I am → Iam → the a falls out → I'm. The apostrophe is the a's little gravestone.

practiceBank.skill: write a contraction with the apostrophe in the gap

block.prompt: Which one shows do not squashed correctly?
block.explain: The o of not drops out, and the apostrophe sits exactly in its place: don't.

wrongAnswers.why: no apostrophe — forgot to mark the missing letter
wrongAnswers.remedy: Compare do not and dont letter by letter — the o of not vanished. How do we mark a vanished letter?

wrongAnswers.why: apostrophe at the join of the words, not where the o dropped
wrongAnswers.remedy: The apostrophe isn't glue between words — it marks the gap. WHICH letter fell out, and where was it sitting?

hints: Write do not, then cross out the letter that disappears.
The o of not goes — the apostrophe takes that exact seat: do n't.

reteach.say: The apostrophe never sits at the join — it sits in the gap. do not: the o of not is buried, so the apostrophe goes between the n and the t: don't.

block.caption: don't — the ' is the o's tiny gravestone

practiceBank.skill: match contractions to their long forms

block.prompt: Match each squashed word to the two words it came from.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: can't→can not, it's→it is, we're→we are, she'll→she will

wrongAnswers.why: guessed the long form instead of un-squashing
wrongAnswers.remedy: Un-squash it out loud: she'll… she wiiill. What did the apostrophe swallow? The w-i of will.

wrongAnswers.why: muddling it's with the belonging word its
wrongAnswers.remedy: It's with an apostrophe is squashed 'it is'. Say 'it is' in its place — does it fit?

hints: Un-squash each one out loud — stretch it back into two words.
The apostrophe shows where letters hid: we're = we a-re… which word lost its a?

reteach.say: Every contraction can be stretched back out. can't → can not. it's → it is. we're → we are. she'll → she will. If you can stretch it back, you know exactly which letters are buried.

practiceBank.skill: write a contraction with the apostrophe in the gap

wrongAnswers.why: dropped the apostrophe — and accidentally made a different word
wrongAnswers.remedy: Careful — were is a whole other word! Which letter of are went missing? Mark its gap.

wrongAnswers.why: kept the a AND added an apostrophe
wrongAnswers.remedy: The apostrophe only appears when a letter LEAVES. Cross out the a of are first — then bury it.

hints: Squash we and are — the a of are falls out.
The apostrophe sits where the a was: we're.

reteach.say: We are → squash → the a of are drops out → we're. And listen: were without the apostrophe is a totally different word — the little gravestone really matters!

practiceBank.skill: identify which letters the apostrophe replaces

block.prompt: she will → she'll. Which letters went missing?
options: the w and i of will
no letters — the words just joined
block.explain: she will squashes to she'll — the w and i of will drop out and the apostrophe marks their spot.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: the w and i of will

wrongAnswers.answer: no letters — the words just joined
wrongAnswers.why: thinks the apostrophe glues words together
wrongAnswers.remedy: Write she will and she'll one above the other. Compare — two letters have vanished. Which ones?

wrongAnswers.why: picked the letters still visible instead of the missing ones
wrongAnswers.remedy: Look at she'll — the two l's are still there at the end! Which letters of will can you NOT see any more?

hints: Line up she will and she'll and compare letter by letter.
The ll survived — so what got buried?

reteach.say: Detective work: she will has s-h-e-w-i-l-l. she'll has s-h-e-'-l-l. The w and the i are gone — and the apostrophe stands guard in their place.

rows: s h e  w i l l

practiceBank.skill: identify which letters the apostrophe replaces

block.statement: In can't, the apostrophe marks where the n and o of not used to be.
block.explain: True — can not loses the n and o, and the apostrophe stands exactly in their place.

wrongAnswers.why: unsure what the apostrophe stands for
wrongAnswers.remedy: Stretch can't back out: can not. Now squash again slowly — watch which letters vanish.

wrongAnswers.answer: True, but it marks the join
wrongAnswers.why: right answer, wrong reason — join-glue idea
wrongAnswers.remedy: It's not glue! Cross out the n and o of not — see how the apostrophe sits exactly in that gap?

hints: Stretch can't back into two words.
can not → cross the n and o → can't.

reteach.say: One more slow-motion squash: can not. The n and o of not fall away, and the apostrophe is their gravestone: can't. Find the missing letters, put the apostrophe there — every single time.

block.caption: cut the n and o… bury them: can't

block.prompt: Write your own sentence using don't or can't — then say which letters the apostrophe buried.
block.sample: I don't like thunder. The apostrophe buried the o of not.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: A sensible sentence with don't/can't spelled correctly, plus naming the buried o (or n and o)

wrongAnswers.why: apostrophe dropped in own writing — the skill hasn't transferred yet
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read your word back — is it squashed from two words? Then letters are missing and need their gravestone.

wrongAnswers.why: wrong-spot apostrophe under pressure
wrongAnswers.remedy: Stop and stretch it back out: do not. Which letter drops? Bury the apostrophe exactly there.

hints: Say your sentence out loud first, then write it.
After writing, stretch your contraction back into two words to check the apostrophe's spot.

reteach.say: Writers double-check contractions by un-squashing: write don't, stretch it to do not, and make sure the apostrophe sits where the missing o was. Try one short sentence about something you love.

block.caption: write it → stretch it back → check the gap

block.prompt: A friend writes do'nt. What went wrong?
options: The apostrophe is at the join, not where the o dropped out
They should write dont with no apostrophe
They squashed the wrong two words
block.explain: The o of not is the missing letter, so the apostrophe belongs between the n and t: don't.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: The apostrophe is at the join, not where the o dropped out

wrongAnswers.why: hasn't anchored WHERE the apostrophe lives
wrongAnswers.remedy: Stretch it back: do not. Cross out the letter that vanishes. Is the apostrophe of do'nt sitting in that gap?

wrongAnswers.why: fixes the wrong thing by deleting the needed apostrophe
wrongAnswers.remedy: A letter really is missing, so we DO need the mark — it's just in the wrong seat. Where should it move to?

hints: The apostrophe must sit exactly in that letter's old seat.

reteach.say: The apostrophe is fussy about its seat. do not loses the o of not — so the apostrophe sits between n and t: don't. At the join (do'nt) it's in the wrong seat entirely.

practiceBank.skill: write a contraction with the apostrophe in the gap

wrongAnswers.why: grabbed a sound-alike word — there means a place
wrongAnswers.remedy: We're squashing two words, so we need an apostrophe for the missing letter. Which option has one?

wrongAnswers.why: another sound-alike — their means belonging
wrongAnswers.remedy: Squashed 'they are' must show its buried a. Look for the word with the little gravestone in it.

hints: Squash they and are — the a of are drops out.
The answer needs an apostrophe where the a was: they're.

reteach.say: they are → squash → the a of are falls out → they're. Watch out: two copycat words SOUND the same — there and their — but only they're has the apostrophe, because only they're is a squash. We'll meet those copycats properly soon!

rows: squashed 'they are' — apostrophe for the lost a

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, mix writing contractions with spotting wrong-spot apostrophes.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach with the slow-motion squash (write both words, cross the dropped letters in red), then a level-1 item.
adaptivity.masterySignal: 3+ correct across levels 2–3 including one placement question (which letters went missing?) and one written contraction → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'apostrophes for contraction'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'let's find which letters fall out.'
Step down: cross the dropped letters together first.
ONE hint: 'the apostrophe goes exactly where you crossed out.'
Re-ask a smaller version (one pair: I am → I'm).
Keep it safe: 'Apostrophes hide where letters used to be — let's hunt for the gap.'
adaptivity.personalization: Build practice sentences around the learner's interests (pets, games, foods) — 'I don't like…', 'We're going to…'. Never change the target contraction.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable squash; praise the process — 'you found the missing letters every time and put the apostrophe right on the spot.'

differentiation.support: Cross out the dropped letters FOR the child first; they just place the apostrophe in the gap. Stay on I'm / don't / it's.
differentiation.stretch: Write they're and you're and say exactly which letters are missing (they are → they're: the a; you are → you're: the a).

extension: Find three contractions in a favourite storybook page and write out the two words each one came from.
assessmentEvidence: Child writes at least three contractions with the apostrophe correctly placed where letters were dropped (e.g. can't, I'm, it's) and can name the buried letters.
revisitLater: Lesson 12 introduces the apostrophe's second job (belonging) — recall this one as the contrast; both return in Lesson 13's 'trap'. they're returns in Lesson 14.
